Harold Lloyd was one of the most popular comedians of the silent film era, and one whose career continued on into talking pictures. People who do not know the name may at least be familiar with the scene from his 1923 movie, Safety Last!, where he hangs from a clock on the side of a skyscraper. https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Safetylast-1.jpg

By the time he shot that film, he had already lost a finger and a thumb to an accident.

On August 24, 1919, he (Harold Lloyd) was posing for a gag photo in which he was lighting a cigarette with the burning wick of a bomb. Although it was thought to be a mere prop, the bomb was all too real. The resulting explosion tore a gaping hole in the sixteen-foot ceiling above him and smashed all the windows in the room. Harold stood dumbstruck. His face was a mass of blood and he was blinded; his right hand was bleeding profusely and part of it appeared to be missing. In fact, he had lost his thumb and his forefinger would be soon be amputated. His eyesight shortly returned to normal, but he had to contend with a long and painful convalescence. When he was finally ready to face the cameras again, he was fitted with a special flesh-toned glove to give the appearance of a complete right hand. His fans did not seem to notice that he was impaired since he continued to perform the daredevil stunts which had become his stock in trade.

Source: Davis, Lon. Silent Lives (p. 228-229). Bear Manor
